body: The experimental C#/.NET warning is appended whenever the editor is built with Mono enabled, even for projects that don’t contain any .csproj/.sln. This can produce a confusing warning for non-C# projects, and `_project_contains_dotnet()` is currently unused.

diff_hunk:
@@ -124,7 +125,7 @@ def configure(env: "SConsEnvironment"):
     env["EXPORTED_RUNTIME_METHODS"] = []
 
     # Validate arch.
-    supported_arches = ["wasm32", "wasm64"]
+    supported_arches = ["wasm32"]
     validate_arch(env["arch"], get_name(), supported_arches)
body: Limiting `supported_arches` to only `wasm32` removes existing `wasm64` web builds (used elsewhere in the repo/CI) for non-.NET exports. If the intent is only to restrict Mono to wasm32, the validation should be conditional on `module_mono_enabled`.

The file-extension ignore checks use `EndsWith(string)` without `StringComparison`, which is culture-sensitive and case-sensitive. This is inconsistent with the surrounding code (which uses `StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase`) and can miss files with uppercase extensions on some systems.

body:
MSBuild's `<Error>` task expects the message in the `Text` attribute (as used below on line 50). Using `Message=` here is likely ignored/invalid and can prevent the build from failing as intended.

This issue also appears on line 54 of the same file.

body: `WriteLinesToFile` uses backslashes in the `File=` path. `mono_configure.py` later expects `bin/<rid>/runtime-pack-dir.txt`, and backslashes can produce an unexpected filename on non-Windows. Use forward slashes for a portable path.

body: The linker flags passed for whole-archive use `-Wl,-whole-archive`/`-Wl,-no-whole-archive` (single dash). The standard GNU/LLD options are `--whole-archive`/`--no-whole-archive` (double dash); using the single-dash form is likely to fail the link step.

This file appears to duplicate `modules/mono/runtime/GetRuntimePack/ManagedCallbacks.cs` (which already contains the unmanaged-callback stubs used by the GetRuntimePack project). Keeping a second copy at the repo root is easy to forget/update and doesn’t appear to be referenced by any project.

`PublishConfig.Archs` was changed from a `HashSet` to a `List`. This loses de-duplication semantics and can cause duplicate `dotnet publish` calls (e.g. when `universal` is combined with explicit arch features). If the change is only to avoid C# collection expressions, you can keep the `HashSet` and initialize it explicitly.

This issue also appears in the following locations of the same file:
- line 231
- line 564
